metaDesc: The best seafood restaurants in Chanthaburi, Thailand — ranked by neighborhood across Chao Lao, Laem Sing and Pak Nam Khaem Nu. Blue crab, tiger prawns, fresh oysters, day-boat fish, with signature dishes, rough prices and hours locals actually use.
keywords: Chanthaburi seafood, Chao Lao seafood, Laem Sing restaurants, Pak Nam Khaem Nu, Chanthaburi blue crab
h1:
Chanthaburi Seafood
10 Top Spots by the Sea
intro: Chanthaburi has a long coastline running from Chao Lao through Laem Sing all the way to Pak Nam Khaem Nu. Small fishing boats head out every morning, so you get firm-meat blue crab, big tiger prawns, plump oysters and fish straight off the boat. We picked 10 places where the catch is genuinely fresh and locals actually eat, grouped by area, with each spot's standout dishes and rough prices.

blocks.html: Seafood is the main reason a lot of people drive to Chanthaburi on a weekend. What stands out here is freshness, because most restaurants buy straight from the local fishing boats that same day, and a few even run their own crab and prawn farms. We've ordered the spots by the three main beach areas so it's easy to plan which direction to head.

blocks.title: Read this first
blocks.html: On long weekends the popular beachfront places get packed, especially around sunset. Call ahead to book a table, or arrive before 5pm to grab a sea-view seat more easily · Prices in this article are rough per-dish estimates and depend on the size of that day's crab and prawns, so always ask the price by weight before you order.

blocks.text: Laem Sing — fresh off the local boats

blocks.html: Laem Sing sits where the Chanthaburi River meets the sea, an old fishing district. Many places here are family-run, the catch comes off the boats nearby, and the standouts are blue crab and seasonal sea fish.

items.name: Krua Ao Mu
items.blurb: Tucked down Soi Ao Mu — drive past the Laem Sing bridge and follow the lane almost to the end. It's a local favorite that flies under the radar. The blue crab meat is white and firm, sweet the way only day-boat crab is, the seafood tom yum is bold and full-flavored, and the bay view is quiet and easygoing.
items.meta: Ao Mu, Laem Sing · Open 11am–9pm (closed Wed) · ~฿300/person
items.price: Steamed blue crab / seafood tom yum

items.name: Krua Rabiang Chan
items.blurb: Right on Laem Sing beach, with both an air-con room and a deck over the water. The menu covers everything — steamed crab, grilled prawns, curry-powder crab, prawns in tamarind sauce and baked mussels. Good for families who want to order a spread and share.

items.name: New Thiew Son Seafood
items.blurb: A long-running spot on Laem Sing beach with seafood straight from Chanthaburi waters, cooked in a simple home style. The standouts are crab curry, grilled prawns and pomfret fried with fish sauce. Prices are friendly and you can sit back to the sound of the waves.
items.price: Crab curry / fish fried with fish sauce

blocks.text: Pak Nam Khaem Nu — oysters and sea farms

blocks.html: Pak Nam Khaem Nu is another river mouth, with the blue temple (Wat Khet Nabun Yaram) as a landmark nearby. This area is known for big oysters and seafood from local farms — a good lunch stop before or after visiting the temple.

items.name: Krua Khun Lho Seafood
items.blurb: On Burapha Chonlathit Road, near the Pak Nam Khaem Nu bridge and the blue temple. The big draw is the restaurant's own seafood farm, so the blue crab, mud crab and tiger prawns are very fresh. There's a cool, glass-walled air-con room with a sea view, and the signatures are soft-shell crab in curry powder and crab with glass noodles.
items.meta: Pak Nam Khaem Nu, Burapha Chonlathit Rd · Open 10am–8:30pm · 5-dish seafood set ~฿1,200
items.price: Crab roe with glass noodles / soft-shell crab in curry powder

items.name: Chill Lay Station
items.blurb: About 2km from Pak Nam Khaem Nu, with an indoor room, a lawn area and a section by the water. The standouts are grouper stir-fried with chili, soft-shell crab in curry powder, and sour curry with fish roe. A good spot to settle in for a while and take photos.

items.name: Krua Maley
items.blurb: A restaurant with a river-mouth view, where the blue water plays off the fishing boats — best in the late afternoon when the light is soft. The catch is fresh and seasonal; order fresh oysters and steamed lime fish to enjoy with the view.
items.meta: Pak Nam Khaem Nu area · River-mouth view

blocks.text: Chao Lao — the popular beachfront strip

blocks.html: Chao Lao beach is in Tha Mai district, about 30km from Chanthaburi town, and it has the most beachfront restaurants — many of them right on the sand. It's a great spot for dinner while you wait for the sunset. It gets crowded on weekends, so come a little early or book ahead.

items.name: Sut Thang Rak Seafood
items.blurb: On Chao Lao beach, with a section right by the water and an open sea view. The usual orders are big firm-meat grilled prawns, plump sweet snails, and fish fried with fish sauce — fresh seafood with the waves rolling in right beside you.
items.meta: Chao Lao beach, Tha Mai · Beachfront seating

items.name: Krua Mar Had Beach
items.blurb: Right on Chao Lao beach, with fresh seafood brought in daily by local fishermen. The standouts are sea bass miang with herbs, soft-shell crab in curry powder, and prawns in tamarind sauce with crispy wonton. The vibe is relaxed and easygoing.

items.name: Pu Ma Chom Talay
items.blurb: A restaurant inside a resort on Chao Lao beach, with relaxed sea views. As the name suggests, it's known for blue crab — order the steamed blue crab with seafood dipping sauce for that fresh-crab flavor. A handy stop between beach time.
items.meta: Chao Lao beach, Tha Mai · Sea-view seating

items.name: Malibu Beach Chao Lao
items.blurb: A beachfront spot where you can eat seafood while looking out over the long stretch of sand, with a chilled beach-club feel and live shows some evenings. Good for a group of friends who want to settle in and listen to the waves into the night.

items: Steamed blue crab — the star of Chanthaburi. White, firm, sweet meat with seafood dipping sauce. Look for meat that fills the shell tightly, and if it has roe, even better value.
Grilled tiger prawns — big and bouncy, and very fresh at the places with their own farms. Grilled just to done, then dipped in seafood sauce or spicy nam jim jaew.
Fresh oysters — big ones from the farms near the river mouth, eaten raw with the usual sides: fried shallots, lime, garlic and chili.
Curry-powder crab / soft-shell crab in curry powder — a dish almost every place does well, fragrant with curry powder and fluffy egg, great over rice.
Pomfret / sea bass fried with fish sauce — fresh fish fried crisp outside and soft inside, finished with sweet-salty fish sauce, eaten with hot steamed rice.

blocks.title: How to pick the freshest catch
blocks.html: Fresh crab has a firm shell, clear dark eyes and legs that still move · fresh prawns have clear shells and heads that aren't darkened · good oysters are plump with clear liquid and no strong fishy smell · if you're not sure, ask which catch just came in that day — you'll usually get the freshest thing available.

If you only have one day, sticking to a single area is the easiest move, since these three areas are in different directions — about 20–40 minutes' drive between them. Below is an unhurried two-day seafood plan.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Laem Sing + Pak Nam Khaem Nu

items.activity: Start with lunch at Krua Ao Mu, Laem Sing
items.note: Order steamed blue crab and seafood tom yum. Arrive before noon and it's not packed yet (closed Wednesdays).

items.activity: Stop by the blue temple, Pak Nam Khaem Nu
items.note: Photogenic blue temple, close to the dinner spot.

items.activity: Dinner at Krua Khun Lho Seafood
items.note: Straight from the restaurant's own farm — order tiger prawns and fresh oysters, sitting in the glass-walled sea-view room.

items.activity: Drive over toward Tha Mai and swim at Chao Lao beach
items.note: Long beach, clear water — take a walk before lunch.

items.activity: Lunch at Krua Mar Had Beach
items.note: Sea bass miang with herbs and soft-shell crab in curry powder, sitting right by the water.

items.activity: Move on to Sut Thang Rak Seafood for sunset
items.note: Big grilled prawns and sweet snails — end the trip with the evening light on the beach.

faq.q: Which Chanthaburi seafood area has the freshest catch?
faq.a: Laem Sing, Pak Nam Khaem Nu and Chao Lao all get fresh catch off the local boats that same day. Laem Sing is strong on blue crab and seasonal sea fish, Pak Nam Khaem Nu on oysters and farm seafood, and Chao Lao has the most beachfront restaurants to choose from. Pick the area closest to your route for an easier trip.

faq.q: Where's the best blue crab in Chanthaburi?
faq.a: Krua Ao Mu in Laem Sing is known for firm, sweet steamed blue crab, while Pu Ma Chom Talay at Chao Lao leans into blue crab as its name suggests. If you prefer crab from a restaurant's own farm, Krua Khun Lho at Pak Nam Khaem Nu has fresh blue crab and mud crab.

faq.q: How much does seafood in Chanthaburi cost?
faq.a: Most dishes run roughly ฿100–400 depending on type and size, and big crab or prawns are priced by weight. Expect to spend around ฿300 or more per person if you order several seafood dishes. Some places have combined seafood sets starting around ฿1,200 for 4–5 people. Always ask the price by weight before ordering big crab or prawns.

faq.q: Should I book a table in advance?
faq.a: On long weekends and around sunset the popular beachfront places get very busy, so it's worth calling to book or arriving before 5pm. On weekdays it's usually easier to grab a sea-view seat.

faq.q: Which restaurants are good for families?
faq.a: Krua Rabiang Chan in Laem Sing has both an air-con room and a deck over the water, with a full menu you can share. Chill Lay Station near Khaem Nu has a lawn area where kids can run around — both work well for a family outing.
